Hierarchical response clustering

Branch geometry uses Ward D2 on all retained standardized, equally block-weighted coordinates. Coloured circles identify statistical groups at the chosen cut. Regime tiles use the separate value-added rule; hover or focus them for signed responses.

Select a named leaf or regime tile to inspect it. Highlighting preserves the full hierarchy.

Principal component analysis

Point colour and solid ovals show Ward groups; dashed ovals show the separate value-added regimes. Each oval encloses its observations in this two-dimensional projection; it is not a confidence region. Ovals can overlap because the clustering uses more than two coordinates. The notes report each Ward group’s regime mix.

    Hover or focus a point for its scenario, closure, setup, cluster and transmission branch.

    Regimes across closures

    Gold, fiat and quasi-float retain the same broad labels within each setup. OPENFIXG changes six EU/RoW labels and one North/South label; North/South Int-Wood also changes SCc to SCw. SCw can include expansion: it requires a weak region-2 response, irrespective of region-1 sign.

    Scenario, setup and closure effects

    Descriptive shares across 96 deterministic experiments: twelve scenarios, two regional setups and four closures, with six equally weighted outcome blocks. The full factorial has no residual degrees of freedom; these are not inferential significance tests.

    Signed response magnitudes

    Display bands in each coordinate’s reported units: +₀/−₀ = nonzero magnitude below 0.003; +/− = 0.003–0.03; ++/−− = 0.03–0.3; +++/−−− = at least 0.3. Exact zero = 0. These display bands do not assign regimes. Hover a cell for its numerical response and units.
